query: Which method can be used for the presence of ferromagnetic ground states, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Mössbauer spectroscopy can be used to detect the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in materials.
generation.intervention: Mössbauer spectroscopy measurement with gamma-ray source and detector
generation.conditions: Low temperature (e.g., 4.2 K) and external magnetic field (e.g., 1 Tesla)
generation.mechanism: Nuclear gamma resonance absorption and emission
generation.predicted_outcome: A minimum of 6% increase in the absorption peak intensity compared to the paramagnetic state, measured in counts per second (cps)
generation.baseline: Paramagnetic state at high temperature (e.g., 300 K)
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 4.2 K to 300 K, Magnetic field range: 0 Tesla to 1 Tesla
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of the measurement may depend on the sample quality, instrument calibration, and data analysis procedures.

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the Mössbauer spectrum of a known ferromagnetic material at low temperature and compare it to the spectrum at high temperature.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the absorption peak intensity increase is less than 3% or the magnetic hyperfine field is not detectable, the hypothesis is falsified.
